sections.content: You know direct object pronouns *lo*, *la*, *los*, and *las* from A2 Unit 12 and indirect object pronouns *le* and *les* from A2 Unit 25. Most of the Spanish-speaking world keeps them distinct by grammatical role: *lo* and *la* replace a direct object (*Ayer vi a Juan → Ayer lo vi*), while *le* replaces an indirect object (*Dije la verdad a María → Le dije la verdad*).

In central and northern Spain, speakers often shift these pronouns by gender and animacy instead of syntactic role. Using *le* as a direct object is called *leísmo*. The RAE academic norm accepts only one specific case: singular *le* referring to a male person (*A Juan le vi ayer* alongside standard *A Juan lo vi ayer*). Using *le* for a thing (*El libro le leí*) or for a woman (*A María le vi*), using *la* as an indirect object for a woman (*laísmo*: *A María la dije la verdad*), and using *lo* as an indirect object (*loísmo*: *A Pedro lo di un regalo*) are all rejected by the shared standard. At C1, you need to recognize these phenomena in peninsular speech and literature while keeping your own production in the standard *lo / la / le* system.

sections.title: Standard Pronouns vs. Leísmo, Laísmo, and Loísmo
rows: A Juan lo vi ayer. / A María la llamé. / El informe lo leí.
A Juan le di el aviso. / A María le dije la verdad.
A Juan le vi ayer en la estación. (= A Juan lo vi ayer.)
*El informe le leí ayer.* → El informe lo leí ayer.
*A María la dije la verdad.* → A María le dije la verdad.
*A Pedro lo di un regalo.* → A Pedro le di un regalo.

items.spanish: En muchas novelas del centro de España se lee «A don Carlos le acompañé hasta la puerta», uso que la norma culta admite.
items.english: In many novels from central Spain one reads 'I accompanied Don Carlos to the door', a usage that the educated norm accepts.

items.spanish: En América y en gran parte de España se prefiere el estándar etimológico: «A don Carlos lo acompañé hasta la puerta».
items.english: In the Americas and in much of Spain the etymological standard is preferred: 'I accompanied Don Carlos to the door'.

items.spanish: Construcciones como «A mi hermana la escribí una carta» son casos de laísmo que deben evitarse en el registro formal.
items.english: Constructions such as 'I wrote my sister a letter' (with 'la') are cases of laísmo that should be avoided in formal register.

items.spanish: Para comprobar si el verbo pide objeto directo o indirecto en el estándar, conviene sustituir por un nombre femenino: «La ayudé» o «Le di las gracias».
items.english: To check whether the verb takes a direct or indirect object in the standard, it is helpful to substitute a feminine noun: 'I helped her' or 'I thanked her'.

sections.content: When analyzing an authentic sentence, check the verb's argument structure first. *Ver*, *llamar*, *acompañar*, and *invitar* take a direct object (*lo / la*, or accepted male-person *le*). *Decir algo a alguien*, *dar algo a alguien*, *escribir algo a alguien*, and *preguntar algo a alguien* already have a direct object (the thing said, given, written, or asked), so the person receiving it is always an indirect object (*le / les*, never *la* or *lo*).
